newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Ford unit 1996 output slips.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Ford unit 1996 output slips.

text.p: Ford Motor Co's Belgian factory said on Tuesday that 1996 production would be lower than a year earlier but was bound to pick up again in 1997.
"I expect that in 1997 we'll sell about the same volume as in 1995," Ford Genk director Peter Heller told Reuters by telephone.
The plant in Genk, northeastern Belgium, built 388,409 Mondeo saloon cars and 82,186 Transit vans in 1995.
Heller estimated that total production for 1996 would slip to 370,000 for the Mondeo and to 68,000 for the Transit.
Production of the Mondeo mainly suffered from its facelift earlier this year, he said.
"The main reason is the introduction of the new Mondeo. In the run-up you always lose cars because you cannot produce the same volume from day one," Heller said.
He said that the impact of the launch of the revamped Mondeo cut production by between 13,000 and 14,000 cars.
Production of the new-look Mondeo began in August but volumes were only back at par again in November.
The output of the Transit van was hit by the introduction of similar models by rivalling car makers.
"The market has been reduced because a few fellow car makers...Fiat and Peugeot and others now also have a comparable model," Heller said.
"They tried to copy the Transit and have partly succeeded. Now the Germans also buy Mercedes," he said.
"But I believe that for the Transit we have now reached rock-bottom," he added.
Production for both models in Genk will be halted on December 23 and was due to resume on January 15.
Last year the plant was only closed between Christmas and New Year but Heller said that the plant was also shut for a number of days in the first two months of this year.
"Last year we were just as much closed," said Heller, noting that the number of closed days for the Transit production would be less at the end of this year than a year ago.
Genk, a division of Ford's German unit Ford Werke AG. exports 96.5 percent of its production and accounts for 40 percent of total car exports from Belgium.
England and Germany soak up 45 percent of total production and are Genk's main markets.
